title: Citizen home prints the server's date, so the browser shows a hydration error and can show the wrong day
what_happens: CitizenHome builds today's date with new Date().toLocaleDateString without a time zone. The server (UTC) and the citizen's browser (IST) disagree between 00:00 and 05:30 IST. In a real browser run, /citizen logged React error 425 several times and the server HTML said 'Friday, 6 November' while the page showed 'Saturday, 7 November'.
what_should_happen: Use the Chennai time zone (Asia/Kolkata) for the date on both sides, so there is no console error and no wrong day.
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/hunt-citizen.test.ts  (hunt-citizen-1, it.fails). Browser: node tests/qa/pass4/with-lock.mjs browser 3 -- node tests/qa/pass4/hunt-citizen.browser.mjs 3175
evidence: docs/qa/pass4/evidence/hunt-citizen.browser.json (errs for /citizen); tests/qa/pass4/hunt-citizen.test.ts. Note: in this run the server clock was frozen at 6 Nov, which made the gap show at any hour; the test shows the real UTC versus IST case.

title: A corrupt or non-Excel file named .xlsx or .csv is called 'empty', not 'unreadable'
what_happens: Uploading the text 'this is not a zip' as a.xlsx, or random bytes as b.csv, gives 'has no rows of data' and the advice 'Ask the department for the full file'. A bad PDF and bad JSON do get a correct 'could not be read' message.
what_should_happen: Say the file could not be opened as an Excel or CSV file, and ask for a fresh copy.
evidence: docs/qa/pass4/evidence/hunt-citizen.corrupt-files.log (real run; no failing it.fails test written, reached out of time)
root_cause_guess: src/lib/studio (reader returns 0 rows instead of an error for a bad xlsx or binary csv)

title: Filing a complaint on a test server writes a row into the tracked dataset files in the repo
what_happens: Each complaint filed through POST /api/complaints on the QA server (dry-run, own data folder) also appended a row to data/datasets/grievances.csv and grievance_status_history.csv, which are tracked in git. 6 complaints gave 6 new rows in each file. I restored both files with git checkout.
what_should_happen: A dry-run or test server must write only to its own data folder. Test complaints must never reach the dataset that Data Studio and the analytics read.
repro: node tests/qa/pass4/server.mjs start --port 3175 --instance x; sign in as citizenA; POST a valid complaint to /api/complaints; git status shows both CSV files modified
evidence: git diff of data/datasets/grievances.csv after node tests/qa/pass4/hunt-citizen.probe6.mjs 3175 (seen in this run, 6 added lines; no it.fails test written)
class: test data leaking into real data
